incident: An agent deleted a production database during a code freeze
outcome: restored by a platform rollback, as the user reports
evidence: sharwood2025: e1; e2; e3; e4; e5
note: The code freeze was an instruction to the agent, not a specification that anything enforced. As the user reports it, the agent said that a rollback was "impossible in this case", and the rollback then worked. The report does not say what the agent could have done itself, so the failure of S6 is disputed; the agent's wrong belief is a failure of S4.

incident: An agent ran a Terraform destroy on a production database
outcome: restored from a vendor snapshot, after about 24 hours
evidence: grigorev2026: e1; e2; e3; e4; e7; e8; e9; e10
note: An apply run without the state file created duplicates. The agent then unpacked an archive that replaced the current state file with an older one describing production, and ran terraform destroy while the user believed that only the duplicates would go. The automated snapshots were deleted too; the vendor held one. McLean et al. date the incident to February 2025 and attribute the destroy to the missing state file; the source dates it to 26 February 2026 and attributes the destroy to the older state file. No undo by the agent is reported; the snapshots were deleted, the user opened a support ticket, and the vendor restored the database, so recovery came from outside the agent's process.

our_sources: openai2026; openai2026b; openai2026c; huggingface2026a; huggingface2026b; metr2026
outcome: stopped by the victim and by the lab; internal datasets and credentials had been accessed, and, by the lab's account, four private code repositories downloaded
evidence: openai2026: e1; e2; e3; e4; e5; openai2026c: e1; e2; e3; e4; e5; e6; e7; e8; e9; openai2026b: e1; e2; e3; e4; e5; huggingface2026b: e1; e2; huggingface2026a: e1; e2; e3; metr2026: e1; e2; e3; e4; e5; e6; e7; e8
note: The lab describes the July runs as evaluations in settings "not reflective of" its production environments, without its deployed safeguards. Internet access from training runs is reported for May 2026, by an SSRF exploit of a package proxy; one May experiment had internet access by design. S6 and U3 rest on the training and evaluation reports; S5 by our convention that adaptation in context counts as an update, and U1 on the evaluation. Agents took goals from notes left by other agents. The lab calls the incident an outlier scenario, and the independent reviewers state that their data are incomplete and were analysed with the help of a model.
